extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and patent office staff in South Africa
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards and procedural requirements under the South African Patents Act for who may practice as patent agents, what inventions are patentable, application filing/formalities, specification contents, priority, examination, refusal grounds, lapsing, public inspection, patent of addition, and PCT national-phase processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to practise as patent agents and patent attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to section 22, no person shall practise as a patent agent or a patent attorney unless he is registered as such under section 20; nor hold himself out as a patent agent or patent attorney or use any words/names/titles/description indicating that he is a patent agent or patent attorney unless he is registered under section 20 or practises as an attorney in partnership with a person registered as a patent attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes exceptions (practising attorney may instruct/correspond with an agent acting merely as intermediary), representation by an employed patent agent, restrictions while removed/suspended from register (cannot practise or be employed in profession-related capacities except with registrar's written consent after notice to the South African Institute of Intellectual Property Law), prohibition on employing removed/suspended persons without registrar's consent, penalties (fine up to R1,000 or imprisonment up to 12 months), registrar/Institute may apply for interdicts, patent agents' communications privileged like attorneys, and patent attorneys deemed to be practising as attorneys for other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be granted for any new invention which involves an inventive step and which is capable of being used or applied in trade or industry or agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core patentability triad: novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability/usefulness (trade/industry/agriculture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (what shall not be an invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything which consists of a discovery; a scientific theory; a mathematical method; a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work or any other aesthetic creation; a scheme, rule or method for performing a mental act, playing a game or doing business; a program for a computer; or the presentation of information, shall not be an invention for the purposes of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection (3) limits this exclusion: these things are excluded only 'to the extent to which a patent or an application for a patent relates to that thing as such.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable on moral or biological-coverage grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be granted for an invention the publication or exploitation of which would be generally expected to encourage offensive or immoral behaviour; nor for any variety of animal or plant or any essentially biological process for the production of animals or plants, not being a micro-biological process or the product of such a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may refuse applications that would encourage offensive/immoral behaviour; special treatment/exceptions exist for microbiological processes/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (when an invention is deemed to be new)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be deemed to be new if it does not form part of the state of the art immediately before the priority date of that invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State of the art includes all matter made available to the public anywhere by written or oral description, by use or any other way, and also matter in earlier patent applications open to public inspection if that matter was contained both as lodged and as open to inspection and has an earlier priority date. Secret commercial use in the Republic also forms part of the state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of the art comprises all matter (product, process, information, or anything else) made available to the public (in the Republic or elsewhere) by written or oral description, by use or any other way; and matter contained in an application open to public inspection where that matter was in the application as lodged and has an earlier priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes secret commercial working within the Republic; special rules apply for matter in patent applications and for evaluating 'fairly based' disclosures when determining priority dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be deemed to involve an inventive step if it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art immediately before the priority date of the invention, having regard to any matter which forms part of the state of the art by virtue only of subsection (6) (and disregarding subsections (7) and (8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step is judged from the perspective of a person skilled in the art, against the state of the art (ordinary public disclosures), with certain disclosures (e.g., later-published applications or secret uses) treated specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of treatment and industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention of a method of treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy or of diagnosis practised on the human or animal body shall be deemed not to be capable of being used or applied in trade or industry or agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, this does not prevent a product (substance or composition) used in such a method from being deemed capable of being used or applied in trade/industry/agriculture merely because it is invented for use in such a method (section 25(12)). Also, a substance/composition forming part of the state of the art does not prevent a patent for a new use in such medical methods if the new use was not part of the state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior knowledge or publication excused in certain circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be invalid solely because the invention or part of it was disclosed, used or known prior to the priority date if (a) the patentee or predecessor proves such knowledge/disclosure/use was acquired or made without his knowledge or consent and was derived from him, and if he learned of it before the priority date that he applied for protection with all reasonable diligence after learning; or (b) it resulted from the invention being worked in the Republic by way of reasonable technical trial or experiment by the applicant/patentee or predecessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are limited exceptions protecting patentees where prior disclosure/use was not attributable to them or where working/experimentation in the Republic caused earlier disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to apply for a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent may be made by the inventor or by any other person acquiring from him the right to apply or by both; in absence of agreement, joint inventors may apply in equal undivided shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets who has legal standing to file; joint applicants default to equal shares unless agreement states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution over rights in inventions or patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a dispute arises as to rights to obtain a patent or to make/use/exercise/dispose of an invention, any such party may apply to the commissioner to decide the matter; the commissioner may order assignments, direct deeds extend to other countries, and may order compensation where just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner empowered to resolve disputes and to take measures (e.g., compel assignments, award compensation) to enable applications to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership of applications (default rules and dispute handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint applicants shall, absent agreement to the contrary, have equal undivided shares and none may deal with the application without consent of other joint applicants; if proceedings are needed to save an application, any applicant may institute such proceedings on behalf of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner can decide disputes about proceeding with or exploiting the application; costs allocation rules and power to order assignments or compensation; commissioner should resolve disputes to preserve the application and lead to grant unless good reasons exist otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and filing requirements for patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be made in the prescribed manner, on payment of the prescribed fee, accompanied by a provisional or complete specification, contain an address for service in the Republic, and be accompanied by a prescribed declaration before acceptance; persons other than inventors must furnish prescribed proof of title/authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications date from lodging; a lodging date shall not be denied on formal grounds only if accompanied by prescribed fee, prescribed signed application form, one copy of the specification in an official language or official language of a convention country, and one copy of drawings (if any), even if drawings not in prescribed form. Translations of specs not in an official language must be furnished within three months, certified to registrar's satisfaction. An application may be amended within two months to claim priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority (conditions and time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete-specification application may claim priority from prior applications (provisional, complete, or convention-country application) provided specified time limits are met (generally within one year, or with prescribed fee within 15 months for certain cases) and other conditions such as being the first application in a convention country and applicant being owner or having acquired right to claim priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed timing and documentary requirements apply; where a subsequent application in a convention country can be deemed the first in limited circumstances (withdrawn/abandoned/refused without public inspection, no priority claimed off it, no rights outstanding). Failure to claim priority within prescribed periods causes lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of specification (provisional and complete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every specification must indicate whether provisional or complete and commence with a title sufficiently indicating subject-matter. A provisional specification shall fairly describe the invention. A complete specification shall have an abstract as prescribed; sufficiently describe, ascertain and, where necessary, illustrate or exemplify the invention and the manner in which it is to be performed to enable a person skilled in the art to perform it; and end with a claim or claims defining the invention for which protection is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of complete specification must relate to a single invention, be clear, and be fairly based on matter disclosed in the specification. Drawings/illustrations must follow prescribed form. For micro-biological inventions requiring a microorganism not publicly available and not obtainable from the specification, the microorganism must be dealt with in the prescribed manner (deposit rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority dates rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority date for an invention or any matter in an application is, except as otherwise provided, the date of lodging of the application; where priority is claimed from earlier applications, priority date is the earliest lodging date in which the invention is fairly based on matter disclosed there; an invention may have one or more priority dates; until contrary proven, priority date is the earliest claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of 'fairly based' involves considering disclosures in all documents lodged with that prior application; new matter introduced by supplementary disclosure has priority equal to lodging date of supplementary disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of applications and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar shall examine in the prescribed manner every application for a patent and every complete specification accompanying such application or lodged in pursuance thereof, and if it complies with the requirements of this Act, he shall accept it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination is statutory and follows prescribed procedures; acceptance follows compliance with Act requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if result of examination is adverse
rubrics_metrics.description: If the result of an examination is adverse to the applicant, the registrar may refuse to accept the application or require the application or specification to be amended in such manner as may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In convention applications, missing prescribed documents may lead registrar to treat the application as an ordinary application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to refuse applications in particular cases (frivolous/illegal/immoral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar shall refuse an application if it appears frivolous (claims anything obviously contrary to well-established natural laws) or if use of the invention would be generally expected to encourage offensive or immoral behaviour. If the invention might be used contrary to law, the registrar may refuse unless the specification is amended by adding a disclaimer or other reference to the illegality as the registrar thinks fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for refusal include scientific impossibility, public morality, and illegality; amendment/disclaimer may salvage otherwise problematic applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application, lodging of fresh application, and post-dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a fresh application is made by the same applicant in respect of part of matter disclosed in an earlier application and before acceptance, the registrar may direct that the fresh application be ante-dated to a date not earlier than the date of the first application. A patent on such fresh application shall not be revoked/invalidated solely because the invention is not new having regard to matter disclosed in the first application. A complete specification may be treated as provisional on applicant's request within 12 months of lodging; applications may be post-dated on request subject to limits (no later than six months from actual lodging or to avoid conflicting priority rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar discretion and strict time limits govern ante-dating, conversion to provisional, and post-dating; priority claim rules constrain post-dating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of addition (how obtained and its effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent for a main invention has been applied for or granted, the applicant/patentee may apply for a patent of addition for any addition, improvement or modification of the main invention. The patent of addition's period is the unexpired portion of the main patent and no renewal fees for it; if main patent is surrendered/revoked/refused/abandoned, the patent of addition may become an independent patent but normal term shall not extend beyond original expiry of main patent. Grant of a patent of addition is conclusive evidence that the invention is a proper subject for such a patent and it will not be revoked solely because it lacks inventive step over the main invention. A main patent and its patent of addition shall not be assignable apart from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of patent of addition can't precede acceptance of main invention's application; various conversion/revocation and fee rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lapsing of applications and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete specification is not accepted within 18 months from date of application, the application shall lapse unless an appeal has been lodged or the appeal period hasn't expired or the delay was not due to any act/omission by the applicant. Registrar shall, on payment of prescribed fee, grant extensions up to three months; on good cause and fee, further extensions may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must monitor acceptance timelines; extensions are limited and discretionary on good cause and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal of specifications in lapsed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no priority was claimed from an application accompanied by a provisional specification and the application has lapsed (or an application and every application claiming priority from it has lapsed/abandoned/finally refused), the registrar shall, at applicant's request in prescribed manner, return any specification lodged in connection with the application, except documents showing proof of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule for applicants to recover specification documents after lapse; financial proof documents retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication of acceptance of complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete specification has been accepted, the registrar shall give written notice to the applicant containing the date of acceptance and a statement that on publication by the applicant in the journal of the acceptance, the patent concerned shall be deemed sealed and granted as from the date of such publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance must be published in the journal within the prescribed period (or further period allowed for good cause on payment) otherwise the application shall lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection by public and access to documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication or after being open for public inspection, the patent and the application and all documents lodged in support shall, on payment of prescribed fee, be open to public inspection in the patent office. When an application claiming priority is open to public inspection, any other application from which it claims priority and supporting documents shall simultaneously be open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After five years from date of application, any person may apply for patentee to supply particulars of any search report issued in another country for an application on same subject-matter; registrar forwards copy to patentee and commissioner can order compliance/enforce orders if patentee fails to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international applications: national-phase commencement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expiry of the applicable PCT period (Article 22 or 39) or prescribed further period, the applicant for an international application designating/electing the Republic shall pay the prescribed national fee to the patent office and, if the international application has not been lodged/published in English, lodge within the prescribed period a translation of the international application containing prescribed contents in an official language of the Republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply within the period results in the international application being deemed abandoned in respect of the Republic; registrar may extend the period up to three months on application; applicant may request early commencement of national processing; during national phase the patent office applies the PCT, its regulations and administrative instructions and other provisions of this Act subject to specified subsections.
